Export all database tables to R

Source: R/database_export.R
databaseExport.Rd

Fetches all tables from the beFAIR SQL database and optionally saves the result as an .rds file. Unlike getDatabase(), this function always queries the database directly — it never reads from a local cache.

Usage

databaseExport(
  path = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  stripped = FALSE,
  replace_missing = TRUE,
  study_ids = NULL,
  remove_id_mapping = TRUE
)

Arguments

path

Character or NULL. Directory where the .rds file should be saved. If NULL, no file is written and the list is returned directly.

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE, an existing .rds file at path is overwritten. If FALSE (default) and the file exists, saving is skipped with a warning.

stripped

Logical. If TRUE, only non-sensitive tables are returned (study-, experiment-, and analysis-level tables, panel tables, event, and publications). Default: FALSE.

replace_missing

Logical. If TRUE, values -999, "N/A", and "N/M" are replaced with NA. Default: TRUE.

study_ids

Character vector or NULL. If provided, only rows linked to these study IDs are retained via filterTableList().

Value

A named list of data frames containing the database tables. If path is provided, the list is also saved as an .rds file in that directory. The filename depends on the parameters used:

  • table_list.rds — default

  • table_list_stripped.rds — when stripped = TRUE

  • table_list_filtered.rds — when study_ids is provided

See also

getDatabase() for a cache-first wrapper around this function.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  # Fetch from DB and return without saving
  data <- databaseExport()

  # Fetch from DB and save to disk
  data <- databaseExport(path = "data/")

  # Force overwrite an existing cache file
  data <- databaseExport(path = "data/", overwrite = TRUE)

  # Fetch stripped dataset for selected studies
  data <- databaseExport(path = "data/", stripped = TRUE, study_ids = c("CHHIL", "ITCHI"))
} # }
